dedupe_keys.name: amlsim synthetic anti money laundering transaction simulator ibm

description: AMLSim is a multi-agent simulator that generates synthetic banking transaction data containing known money-laundering patterns, such as fan-in, fan-out, cycles and scatter-gather typologies, so that detection methods can be trained and tested on labelled data without exposing real customer records. It is developed by IBM Research and published in the IBM organisation's repository, with a wiki describing configuration. Coverage is generic: users set the numbers of accounts, the transaction network and the patterns to inject. The code runs on Java 8 with the MASON agent-based simulation library, with Python 3.7 and NetworkX scripts that build the transaction graph, and it is free under the Apache 2.0 licence; at access the repository had 237 commits, 397 stars and 125 forks. Caveats: the data are synthetic and their realism depends on the parameters chosen, and the dependency versions are old, so it is marked maintained, not active. For simulation it is an agent-based model of transaction networks that can be adapted to test how financial crime detection and payment monitoring respond to scenarios, and it supplies benchmark data for graph analytics. It is related to the Reserve Bank of Australia payments data record in this catalogue, which gives real aggregate payment volumes.
